Title: Cleanup: session state helpers, amend -m fix, transition logging (ENT-221)
State: OPEN
Body:
## Summary

- **Replace `current_session` file** with `FindMostRecentSession()` — eliminates the file-based session tracking mechanism in favor of querying session state files directly
- **Fix non-interactive `git commit --amend -m`** silently dropping checkpoint trailer — detects `isRestoringExisting` (PendingCheckpointID or LastCheckpointID set) and skips the TTY prompt that would fail silently in non-interactive environments (e.g., Claude doing amends)
- **Add `TransitionAndLog()`** as single entry point for all 6 state machine transition call sites, with consistent INFO logging for phase changes and DEBUG for no-ops
- **Fix Gemini parity** — add missing `EventTurnEnd` transition in `handleGeminiAfterAgent` via shared `transitionSessionTurnEnd()` helper
- **Add `entire sessions fix`** command for recovering stuck sessions (active+stale or ended+uncondensed)
- **Enhance `entire reset`** with `--session` flag for targeted reset and active session guards
- **Add integration tests** for commit-before-stop (ACTIVE → ACTIVE_COMMITTED → IDLE) and amend-preserves-trailer flows
- **Add table-driven unit test** for PendingCheckpointID reuse across `source=""` and `source="message"` paths

## Test plan

- [x] `mise run fmt` — clean
- [x] `mise run lint` — 0 issues
- [x] `mise run test:ci` — all unit + integration tests pass
- [x] New unit test `TestPrepareCommitMsg_PendingCheckpointIDReuse` covers both `source=""` and `source="message"` paths
- [x] New integration tests `TestShadow_CommitBeforeStop` and `TestShadow_AmendPreservesTrailer`
- [ ] Manual: verify `git commit --amend -m` preserves trailer in a real session

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## PR Stack (ENT-221)
> **5 of 5** ← you are here
> 1. #168 — Pure session phase state machine
> 2. #169 — Consolidate session state types + transcript simplification
> 3. #170 — Wire state machine into hooks

   141→// extractGeminiMetadata extracts prompts, summary, and modified files from transcript.
   142→func extractGeminiMetadata(ctx *geminiSessionContext) error {

   172→	ctx.modifiedFiles = modifiedFiles

   174→	lastPrompt := ""

   184→// commitGeminiSession commits the session changes using the strategy.
   185→func commitGeminiSession(ctx *geminiSessionContext) error {
   186→	repoRoot, err := paths.RepoRoot()
   187→	if err != nil {
   188→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get repo root: %w", err)
   189→	}
   190→
   191→	preState, err := LoadPrePromptState(ctx.sessionID)
   192→	if err != nil {
   193→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to load pre-prompt state: %v\n", err)
   194→	}
   195→	if preState != nil {
   196→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Loaded pre-prompt state: %d pre-existing untracked files, start message index: %d\n", len(preState.UntrackedFiles), preState.StartMessageIndex)
   197→	}
   198→
   199→	// Get transcript position from pre-prompt state
   200→	var startMessageIndex int
   201→	if preState != nil {
   202→		startMessageIndex = preState.StartMessageIndex
   203→	}
   204→
   205→	// Calculate token usage for this prompt/response cycle (Gemini-specific)
   206→	var tokenUsage *agent.TokenUsage
   207→	if ctx.transcriptPath != "" {
   208→		usage, tokenErr := geminicli.CalculateTokenUsageFromFile(ctx.transcriptPath, startMessageIndex)
   209→		if tokenErr != nil {
   210→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to calculate token usage: %v\n", tokenErr)
   211→		} else if usage != nil && usage.APICallCount > 0 {
   212→			tokenUsage = usage
   213→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Token usage for this checkpoint: input=%d, output=%d, cache_read=%d, api_calls=%d\n",
   214→				tokenUsage.InputTokens, tokenUsage.OutputTokens, tokenUsage.CacheReadTokens, tokenUsage.APICallCount)
   215→		}
   216→	}
   217→
   218→	// Compute new and deleted files (single git status call)
   219→	newFiles, deletedFiles, err := ComputeFileChanges(preState)
   220→	if err != nil {
   221→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to compute file changes: %v\n", err)
   222→	}
   223→
   224→	relModifiedFiles := FilterAndNormalizePaths(ctx.modifiedFiles, repoRoot)
   225→	relNewFiles := FilterAndNormalizePaths(newFiles, repoRoot)
   226→	relDeletedFiles := FilterAndNormalizePaths(deletedFiles, repoRoot)
   227→
   228→	totalChanges := len(relModifiedFiles) + len(relNewFiles) + len(relDeletedFiles)
   229→	if totalChanges == 0 {
   230→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "No files were modified during this session\n")
   231→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Skipping commit\n")
   232→		if cleanupErr := CleanupPrePromptState(ctx.sessionID); cleanupErr != nil {
   233→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to cleanup pre-prompt state: %v\n", cleanupErr)
   234→		}
   235→		return nil
   236→	}
   237→
   238→	logFileChanges(relModifiedFiles, relNewFiles, relDeletedFiles)
   239→
   240→	contextFile := filepath.Join(ctx.sessionDirAbs, paths.ContextFileName)
   241→	if err := createContextFileForGemini(contextFile, ctx.commitMessage, ctx.sessionID, ctx.allPrompts, ctx.summary); err != nil {
   242→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create context file: %w", err)
   243→	}
   244→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Created context file: %s\n", ctx.sessionDir+"/"+paths.ContextFileName)
   245→
   246→	author, err := GetGitAuthor()
   247→	if err != nil {
   248→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get git author: %w", err)
   249→	}
   250→
   251→	strat := GetStrategy()
   252→	if err := strat.EnsureSetup(); err != nil {
   253→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to ensure strategy setup: %v\n", err)
   254→	}
   255→
   256→	// Get agent type from the hook agent (determined by which hook command is running)
   257→	// This is authoritative - if we're in "entire hooks gemini session-end", it's Gemini CLI
   258→	hookAgent, agentErr := GetCurrentHookAgent()
   259→	if agentErr != nil {
   260→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get agent: %w", agentErr)
   261→	}
   262→	agentType := hookAgent.Type()
   263→
   264→	// Get transcript identifier at start from pre-prompt state
   265→	var transcriptIdentifierAtStart string
   266→	if preState != nil {
   267→		transcriptIdentifierAtStart = preState.LastTranscriptIdentifier
   268→	}
   269→
   270→	saveCtx := strategy.SaveContext{
   271→		SessionID:                ctx.sessionID,
   272→		ModifiedFiles:            relModifiedFiles,
   273→		NewFiles:                 relNewFiles,
   274→		DeletedFiles:             relDeletedFiles,
   275→		MetadataDir:              ctx.sessionDir,
   276→		MetadataDirAbs:           ctx.sessionDirAbs,
   277→		CommitMessage:            ctx.commitMessage,
   278→		TranscriptPath:           ctx.transcriptPath,
   279→		AuthorName:               author.Name,
   280→		AuthorEmail:              author.Email,
   281→		AgentType:                agentType,
   282→		StepTranscriptStart:      startMessageIndex,
   283→		StepTranscriptIdentifier: transcriptIdentifierAtStart,
   284→		TokenUsage:               tokenUsage,
   285→	}
   286→
   287→	if err := strat.SaveChanges(saveCtx); err != nil {
   288→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to save session: %w", err)
   289→	}
   290→
   291→	if cleanupErr := CleanupPrePromptState(ctx.sessionID); cleanupErr != nil {
   292→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to cleanup pre-prompt state: %v\n", cleanupErr)
   293→	}
   294→
   295→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Session saved successfully\n")
   296→	return nil
   297→}

   299→// logFileChanges logs the modified, new, and deleted files to stderr.
   300→func logFileChanges(modified, newFiles, deleted []string) {
   301→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Files modified during session (%d):\n", len(modified))
   302→	for _, file := range modified {
   303→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "  - %s\n", file)
   304→	}
   305→	if len(newFiles) > 0 {
   306→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "New files created (%d):\n", len(newFiles))
   307→		for _, file := range newFiles {
   308→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "  - %s\n", file)
   309→		}
   310→	}
   311→	if len(deleted) > 0 {
   312→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Files deleted (%d):\n", len(deleted))
   313→		for _, file := range deleted {
   314→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "  - %s\n", file)
   315→		}
   316→	}
   317→}

   343→	return commitGeminiSession(ctx)

   346→// createContextFileForGemini creates a context.md file for Gemini sessions.
   347→func createContextFileForGemini(contextFile, commitMessage, sessionID string, prompts []string, summary string) error {

   350→	sb.WriteString("# Session Context\n\n")

   358→		}
   359→	}

   361→	if summary != "" {

   367→	if err := os.WriteFile(contextFile, []byte(sb.String()), 0o600); err != nil {
   368→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to write context file: %w", err)
   369→	}
   370→	return nil
   371→}

Good catch on both points. Looking at `handleGeminiSessionEnd()` (line 34-62):

1. **`entireSessionID` naming** — yeah, looks like a leftover from the old `current_session` file approach. The variable should just be `sessionID`.

2. **Can get sessionID from hook payload** — `parseGeminiSessionEnd()` (line 78) already parses `input.SessionID` from stdin. But `handleGeminiSessionEnd()` calls `commitWithMetadataGemini()` which consumes stdin first, then falls back to `FindMostRecentSession()` because stdin is gone. That's the root issue — stdin is consumed by the commit path.

However, `commitWithMetadataGemini()` internally calls `parseGeminiSessionEnd()` which already has `input.SessionID`. The session ID could be returned from that call chain instead of re-discovering it.

There are also several Gemini-specific PRs open:
- **#167** — Fix Gemini transcript position tracking
- **#162** — Skip checkpoint on /quit if session already condensed
- **#158** — Fix Gemini tokenUsage in metadata.json

These look related. Want me to check if #162 (skip checkpoint on /quit) specifically addresses this `handleGeminiSessionEnd` flow? That PR might already be refactoring how session-end works, which would overlap with fixing this here.

Here's the picture:

**PR #162** — Adds a check in `commitWithMetadataGemini()` to skip duplicate checkpoints on `/quit` after a git commit already condensed. It reads session state but still has the same stdin-consumption architecture.

**PR #167** — Fixes transcript line counting for Gemini JSON format in the condensation path. No stdin changes.

None of the three PRs address the fundamental issue you're pointing at: **`handleGeminiSessionEnd` consumes stdin via `commitWithMetadataGemini()`, then has to fall back to `FindMostRecentSession()` to get the session ID for marking the session as ended.**

The fix should be straightforward — `parseGeminiSessionEnd()` (called inside `commitWithMetadataGemini`) already reads `input.SessionID` from stdin. It just needs to be surfaced back up to `handleGeminiSessionEnd()`. Either:

1. Parse stdin once at the top of `handleGeminiSessionEnd()`, then pass the parsed context down to `commitWithMetadataGemini()`
2. Have `commitWithMetadataGemini()` return the session ID it parsed

This would eliminate both the `FindMostRecentSession()` fallback and the `entireSessionID` naming. Want me to fix this as part of this PR, or track it separately?

Perfect! Now I have all the information I need. Let me create a comprehensive summary document:

## Gemini Session-End Handler Flow - Complete Analysis

I've thoroughly explored the codebase and can now provide you with a comprehensive understanding of the Gemini session-end handler flow and related components.

### 1. **Gemini Session-End Handler Flow** (`handleGeminiSessionEnd()` → `commitWithMetadataGemini()` → `parseGeminiSessionEnd()`)

#### Flow Overview (lines 34-62 in hooks_geminicli_handlers.go):

```
handleGeminiSessionEnd()
  ├─ commitWithMetadataGemini()          [parses stdin + commits metadata]
  │   ├─ ShouldSkipOnDefaultBranchForStrategy()  [skip on main/master if strategy doesn't allow]
  │   ├─ parseGeminiSessionEnd()         [consumes stdin, extracts session_id + transcript path]
  │   ├─ setupGeminiSessionDir()         [creates .entire/metadata/session-id/ directory]
  │   ├─ extractGeminiMetadata()         [parses transcript for prompts, summary, files]
  │   └─ commitGeminiSession()           [calls strategy.SaveChanges()]
  │
  └─ markSessionEnded(sessionID)         [uses FindMostRecentSession() since stdin consumed]
      └─ strategy.TransitionAndLog()     [IDLE/ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED → ENDED via state machine]
```

#### Key Design Points:

**stdin consumption:** `commitWithMetadataGemini()` calls `parseGeminiSessionEnd()` which reads and parses stdin via `ag.ParseHookInput(agent.HookSessionEnd, os.Stdin)`. This **consumes stdin entirely**. 

**After stdin consumed:** Line 48 calls `strategy.FindMostRecentSession()` to find the session ID, **since stdin has already been read and cannot be read again**. This is why `handleGeminiSessionEnd` performs both parsing AND cleanup - it's all done in one go.

**Fallback for unknown sessions:** If sessionID is empty, it defaults to `unknownSessionID` (line 99).

---

### 2. **handleGeminiAfterAgent() vs handleGeminiSessionEnd() - Key Differences**

#### handleGeminiAfterAgent() (lines 489-554):

```go
handleGeminiAfterAgent()
  ├─ ShouldSkipOnDefaultBranchForStrategy()    [same skip check]
  ├─ ag.ParseHookInput(agent.HookStop, stdin)  [reads stdin for session_id + transcript]
  ├─ Create geminiSessionContext with parsed data
  ├─ setupGeminiSessionDir()                   [same setup]
  ├─ extractGeminiMetadata()                   [same extraction]
  ├─ commitGeminiSession()                     [same commit]
  └─ transitionSessionTurnEnd(sessionID)       [ACTIVE → IDLE]
      └─ EventTurnEnd event (different from SessionStop!)
```

#### handleGeminiSessionEnd() (lines 34-62):

```go
handleGeminiSessionEnd()
  ├─ commitWithMetadataGemini()                [parses + commits all-in-one]
  │   └─ parseGeminiSessionEnd()
  │       └─ ag.ParseHookInput(agent.HookSessionEnd, stdin)  [reads stdin]
  │
  └─ FindMostRecentSession()                   [AFTER stdin consumed, finds the session]
      └─ markSessionEnded(sessionID)
          └─ EventSessionStop event (different phase change!)
```

#### Critical Difference:

- **AfterAgent** fires **after each prompt/response cycle** and creates checkpoints regularly (equivalent to Claude Code's Stop hook)
- **SessionEnd** fires **once when user explicitly exits** and uses `FindMostRecentSession()` because stdin was already consumed
- **AfterAgent** transitions `ACTIVE → IDLE` (turn ends, but session continues)
- **SessionEnd** transitions to `ENDED` phase (entire session closes)

The comment at lines 30-33 is explicit: *"Note: The primary checkpoint creation happens in AfterAgent (equivalent to Claude's Stop). SessionEnd serves as a cleanup/fallback."*

---

### 3. **handleSessionStartCommon()** and **markSessionEnded()**

#### handleSessionStartCommon() (lines 242-294 in hooks.go):

```go
handleSessionStartCommon()
  ├─ GetCurrentHookAgent()
  ├─ ag.ParseHookInput(agent.HookSessionStart, stdin)
  ├─ Log session start
  ├─ Check for concurrent sessions via strategy.ConcurrentSessionChecker
  ├─ outputHookResponse() to stdout (sends JSON response to agent)
  │
  └─ Load existing session state (if session was previously ended)
      ├─ strategy.LoadSessionState(sessionID)
      └─ strategy.TransitionAndLog(state, session.EventSessionStart, ...)
          └─ ENDED → IDLE (re-entering a closed session resumes it)
```

#### markSessionEnded() (lines 756-775 in hooks_claudecode_handlers.go):

```go
markSessionEnded(sessionID)
  ├─ strategy.LoadSessionState(sessionID)
  ├─ strategy.TransitionAndLog(state, session.EventSessionStop, ...)  [state machine event]
  ├─ Set state.EndedAt = time.Now()           [timestamp when session ended]
  └─ strategy.SaveSessionState(state)
```

The state machine applies `ActionUpdateLastInteraction` and transitions to `PhaseEnded`.

---

### 4. **transitionSessionTurnEnd()** (lines 738-754)

```go
transitionSessionTurnEnd(sessionID)
  ├─ strategy.LoadSessionState(sessionID)
  ├─ strategy.TransitionAndLog(state, session.EventTurnEnd, ...)
  │   └─ ACTIVE → IDLE  (or ACTIVE_COMMITTED → IDLE with ActionCondense)
  └─ strategy.SaveSessionState(state)
```

This is called by **both** `handleGeminiAfterAgent()` (line 551) **and** `commitWithMetadata()` in Claude Code (line 374), signaling the end of a turn/prompt-response cycle, **not** the end of the entire session.

---

### 5. **FindMostRecentSession()** - How It Works (strategy/session_state.go, lines 120-152)

```go
FindMostRecentSession() string
  └─ strategy.ListSessionStates()              [reads all session state files from .git/entire-sessions/]
      ├─ Loop through all states
      ├─ Find state with most recent LastInteractionTime
      ├─ If none have LastInteractionTime, fall back to most recent StartedAt
      └─ Return SessionID (or "" if no sessions exist)
```

**Key insight:** This function finds "the current session" by looking at metadata timestamps, **not by reading user input**. It's used when you can't rely on the agent to pass the session ID (like after stdin was consumed).

**Where it's called:**
- `handleGeminiSessionEnd()` line 48 - to find session after stdin consumed
- Nowhere else in the hooks code (checked via grep)

---

### 6. **Session Phase State Machine** (session/phase.go)

The phases form a lifecycle:

```
IDLE
  ↓ (TurnStart) → ACTIVE
           ↓ (GitCommit while ACTIVE) → ACTIVE_COMMITTED
           ↓ (TurnEnd) → IDLE

ENDED (when user explicitly closes session via SessionStop)
  ↓ (TurnStart) → ACTIVE (re-opening ended session)
```

**Critical transitions for our flow:**
- `IDLE + EventSessionStart → IDLE` (no-op, session already started)
- `ACTIVE + EventTurnEnd → IDLE` (session continues waiting for next prompt)
- `ACTIVE + EventSessionStop → ENDED` (session closed)
- `IDLE + EventSessionStop → ENDED` (session closed from idle)

Actions emitted:
- `ActionUpdateLastInteraction` - updates LastInteractionTime
- `ActionCondense` - prepare metadata for storage (strategy-specific)
- `ActionMigrateShadowBranch` - if git HEAD changed during session

---

### 7. **Type Alignment: SessionState**

In `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_types.go` line 28:

```go
type SessionState = session.State
```

This is a **type alias**, not a new struct. So:
- `SessionState` in the strategy package = `session.State` from session package
- Both refer to the exact same struct
- Stored in `.git/entire-sessions/{session-id}.json`
- Contains: SessionID, Phase, BaseCommit, FilesTouched, EndedAt, LastInteractionTime, etc.

---

### 8. **Claude Code vs Gemini CLI - Handler Comparison**

#### Claude Code handlers (hooks_claudecode_handlers.go):

1. **UserPromptSubmit hook** → `captureInitialState()` + `parseAndLogHookInput()`
2. **Stop hook** → `commitWithMetadata()` 
   - Parses stdin
   - Extracts transcript
   - Calls strategy.SaveChanges()
   - Calls `transitionSessionTurnEnd()`
3. **SessionEnd hook** → `handleClaudeCodeSessionEnd()`
   - Parses stdin (has session_id)
   - Calls `markSessionEnded()` (session → ENDED)

#### Gemini CLI handlers (hooks_geminicli_handlers.go):

1. **BeforeAgent hook** → `handleGeminiBeforeAgent()`
   - Parses stdin
   - Initializes session state via strategy
2. **AfterAgent hook** → `handleGeminiAfterAgent()`
   - Parses stdin
   - Calls `commitGeminiSession()`
   - Calls `transitionSessionTurnEnd()`
   - (Similar to Claude's Stop hook)
3. **SessionEnd hook** → `handleGeminiSessionEnd()`
   - Calls `commitWithMetadataGemini()` (parses + commits)
   - Uses `FindMostRecentSession()` to find session ID
   - Calls `markSessionEnded()` (session → ENDED)

**Pattern:** Both agents have SessionStart, AfterAgent/Stop (for checkpoints), SessionEnd (for cleanup).

---

### 9. **How stdin is consumed and recovered**

**In Gemini handlers:**

```
handleGeminiSessionEnd()
  ├─ commitWithMetadataGemini()
  │   └─ parseGeminiSessionEnd()
  │       └─ ag.ParseHookInput(HookSessionEnd, os.Stdin)  ← STDIN CONSUMED HERE
  │
  └─ FindMostRecentSession()  ← CANNOT READ STDIN, so use state files instead
```

This is why the comment says stdin is consumed (line 42): `commitWithMetadataGemini()` reads all of stdin to parse the hook input, and there's nothing left for `markSessionEnded()` to read.

**Recovery strategy:** Use `strategy.ListSessionStates()` which reads `.git/entire-sessions/*.json` files to find the most recent session by timestamp.

---

### 10. **Key Files Summary**

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `hooks_geminicli_handlers.go` | Gemini-specific hook implementations |
| `hooks_claudecode_handlers.go` | Claude Code-specific hook implementations |
| `hooks.go` | Shared hook utilities (`handleSessionStartCommon()`, etc.) |
| `strategy/session_state.go` | Load/save/list session state files from `.git/entire-sessions/` |
| `strategy/manual_commit_types.go` | Type alias: `SessionState = session.State` |
| `session/state.go` | Session state struct (`State`) and state store (`StateStore`) |
| `session/phase.go` | Phase state machine (phases, events, transitions, actions) |

---

### Summary: The Complete Picture

**commitWithMetadataGemini() does:**
1. Parse session-end hook input (consumes stdin)
2. Create metadata directory
3. Extract prompts, summary, modified files from transcript
4. Create context.md file
5. Call strategy.SaveChanges() to commit the session data

**handleGeminiSessionEnd() then does:**
1. Execute commitWithMetadataGemini() 
2. Use FindMostRecentSession() to get the session ID (since stdin is consumed)
3. Call markSessionEnded() to transition session → ENDED phase

**AfterAgent does similar work but without the SessionEnd wrapper, and only transitions ACTIVE → IDLE** (not the entire session to ENDED).

The state machine handles phase progression; hooks handle data capture and state transitions.

## Approved Plan:
# Inline `commitWithMetadataGemini()` into `handleGeminiSessionEnd()`

## Context

`handleGeminiSessionEnd()` calls `commitWithMetadataGemini()` which consumes stdin internally via `parseGeminiSessionEnd()`. After it returns, `handleGeminiSessionEnd()` can't read stdin anymore, so it falls back to `FindMostRecentSession()` (a timestamp-based heuristic) to find the session ID for `markSessionEnded()`. This is fragile in concurrent multi-session scenarios.

Claude Code's equivalent (`handleClaudeCodeSessionEnd`) is clean: parse stdin once, use `input.SessionID` directly. Gemini should follow the same pattern.

`commitWithMetadataGemini()` has exactly one caller and no reason to exist as a separate function.

## Changes

### File: `cmd/entire/cli/hooks_geminicli_handlers.go`

1. **Inline `commitWithMetadataGemini()` into `handleGeminiSessionEnd()`**:
   - Move the default-branch skip check to the top of `handleGeminiSessionEnd()`
   - Parse stdin once at the top (via `parseGeminiSessionEnd()`)
   - Use `ctx.sessionID` for both the commit path and `markSessionEnded()`
   - Remove the `FindMostRecentSession()` call
   - Remove the `entireSessionID` variable
   - Remove the `commitWithMetadataGemini()` function entirely

2. **Resulting `handleGeminiSessionEnd()` flow**:
   ```
   handleGeminiSessionEnd()
     ├─ ShouldSkipOnDefaultBranchForStrategy()
     ├─ parseGeminiSessionEnd()              [parse stdin once]
     ├─ setupGeminiSessionDir()
     ├─ extractGeminiMetadata()
     ├─ commitGeminiSession()                [best-effort, warn on error]
     └─ markSessionEnded(ctx.sessionID)      [uses parsed session ID directly]
   ```

3. **Rename `entireSessionID`** — eliminated entirely, use `ctx.sessionID` from the parsed input.

### File: `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/session_state.go`

No changes needed. `FindMostRecentSession()` may still have other uses or future uses — leave it for now.

## Verification

```bash
mise run fmt && mise run lint && mise run test:ci
```

The interesting part is the post-commit hook. Let me look at the log lines:

1. **Stop** (21:51:50): Session `28c304f6` saves checkpoint, ACTIVE → IDLE. Normal.
2. **user-prompt-submit** (21:52:15): Same session IDLE → ACTIVE. Normal.
3. **prepare-commit-msg** (21:52:19): Adds trailer. Normal.
4. **post-commit** (21:52:19): Here's the issue:
   - `28c304f6` transitions ACTIVE → ACTIVE_COMMITTED (correct)
   - `446f6b3c` transitions `from="" to=idle` — stale session with empty phase
   - `53a5d919` transitions `from="" to=idle` — stale session with empty phase
   - `bc8f40a7` transitions `from="" to=idle` — stale session with empty phase

The post-commit hook is iterating **all** session states and firing `GitCommit` on each. Three old sessions (pre-state-machine, empty phase) are being woken up and transitioned to IDLE on every commit.

Let me check the post-commit handler to understand the iteration logic.

> AGENT

Here's the full picture:

1. **`findSessionsForWorktree`** returns ALL sessions matching the worktree — no phase filter
2. **`PostCommit`** iterates all of them and fires `EventGitCommit` on each
3. Three stale sessions (`446f6b3c`, `53a5d919`, `bc8f40a7`) have **empty phase** (`""`)
4. `Transition()` normalizes `""` → `PhaseIdle` via `PhaseFromString`
5. `transitionFromIdle(EventGitCommit, ...)` transitions to `PhaseIdle` (no-op in terms of phase) but the log shows `from="" to=idle` because `TransitionAndLog` compares `oldPhase` (which is `""`) with `result.NewPhase` (which is `idle`) — they differ, so it logs as a transition

So the issue is twofold:
- **Noisy**: stale sessions with empty phase generate spurious "phase transition" INFO logs on every commit
- **Wasteful**: they're being processed (content checks, state saves) unnecessarily

The stale sessions are likely old ones that were created before the state machine existed and never got cleaned up or marked as `ENDED`. Should these be filtered out in `findSessionsForWorktree`, or should `PostCommit` skip sessions with empty phase, or should the backward compat normalization happen earlier (at load time) so the log doesn't show `from=""`?

Then... nothing. No stop hook fires after the commit. The session is stuck in `ACTIVE_COMMITTED`. Without the stop hook, there's no `TurnEnd` event, so it never transitions to IDLE and condensation never happens.

OK so `handleClaudeCodeSessionEnd` passes `input.SessionID` (which is Claude Code's model session ID `1bb9c7d2`) to `markSessionEnded()`. But our session state files are keyed by the Entire session ID — which for Claude Code sessions, IS the model session ID (Claude Code passes its session UUID through `UserPromptSubmit`, and that's what `InitializeSession` uses).

But looking at the log: `session_id=28c304f6` appears alongside `model_session_id=1bb9c7d2`. The `session_id` field is coming from the logging context, not from `handleClaudeCodeSessionEnd`. It's the log file routing (from `initHookLogging → FindMostRecentSession`).

So the actual `markSessionEnded("1bb9c7d2")` call either:
- Failed silently because there's no state file for `1bb9c7d2` (it was a different, untracked session)
- Or succeeded if `1bb9c7d2` does have a state file

Either way, session `28c304f6` — the one stuck in ACTIVE_COMMITTED — was never marked as ended, and its stop hook never fired.

**Summary of the three issues found:**

1. **Stale sessions with empty phase** get processed on every commit (noisy `from="" to=idle` transitions)
2. **Log file routing uses `FindMostRecentSession()`** — writes to wrong session's log when multiple sessions exist
3. **Missing stop hook** — session `28c304f6` is stuck in ACTIVE_COMMITTED because Claude Code's stop hook never fired after the agent's turn ended with a git commit

\#3 is likely a Claude Code behavior issue (not our code), but #1 and #2 are ours. Want to tackle these, or focus on understanding #3 first?

Here's what happened: the post-commit hook (21:52:19) ran `TransitionAndLog` on all 4 sessions, including the 3 stale ones. `ApplyCommonActions` set `LastInteractionTime` on each. {"id":"2ceb7a6b-f396-4683-b59c-8d3d8005eb05","identifier":"ENT-250","title":"Introduce ActionHandler interface for compile-time exhaustive action dispatch","description":"## Problem\n\nThe state machine in `session/phase.go` returns `[]Action` from `ApplyCommonActions`, and callers (e.g., `PostCommit` in `manual_commit_hooks.go`) must dispatch each action in a `switch`. This pattern has two silent-drop risks:\n\n1. **Framework gap**: `ApplyCommonActions` (line 299) routes actions to either \"apply internally\" or \"pass through as `remaining`\". Its switch has no `default` — a new action not listed in either arm silently vanishes before the caller ever sees it.\n2. **Caller gap**: The caller's dispatch loop also has no exhaustiveness guarantee. Go's `exhaustive` linter (already enabled) catches missing `case` arms, but only if the action reaches the caller in the first place (see #1).\n\nAdding a new `Action` constant requires updating **both** the framework routing and every caller's switch. There's no compile-time enforcement — you discover the miss at runtime (or never, if it's a silent no-op).\n\nThis was surfaced during PR #172 review while fixing a condensation-failure bug in the PostCommit dispatch loop.\n\n## Proposed Solution: `ActionHandler` interface\n\nInvert control so the framework **calls the caller** instead of returning a bag of actions:\n\n```go\n// ActionHandler defines strategy-specific side effects for state transitions.\n// The framework calls these during ApplyTransition — the compiler enforces\n// that every strategy-specific action has a handler.\ntype ActionHandler interface {\n    HandleCondense(state *State) error\n    HandleCondenseIfFilesTouched(state *State) error\n    HandleDiscardIfNoFiles(state *State) error\n    HandleMigrateShadowBranch(state *State) error\n    HandleWarnStaleSession(state *State) error\n}\n```\n\nReplace `ApplyCommonActions` with `ApplyTransition`:\n\n```go\nfunc ApplyTransition(state *State, result TransitionResult, handler ActionHandler) error {\n    state.Phase = result.NewPhase\n    for _, action := range result.Actions {\n        switch action {\n        case ActionUpdateLastInteraction:\n            now := time.Now()\n            state.LastInteractionTime = &now\n        case ActionClearEndedAt:\n            state.EndedAt = nil\n        case ActionCondense:\n            if err := handler.HandleCondense(state); err != nil { return err }\n        case ActionCondenseIfFilesTouched:\n            if err := handler.HandleCondenseIfFilesTouched(state); err != nil { return err }\n        // ... remaining strategy-specific actions\n        }\n    }\n    return nil\n}\n```\n\nCallers construct a handler struct that captures per-invocation context:\n\n```go\ntype postCommitActionHandler struct {\n    s                      *ManualCommitStrategy\n    logCtx                 context.Context\n    repo                   *git.Repository\n    checkpointID           string\n    // ... other per-call context\n}\n\nfunc (h *postCommitActionHandler) HandleCondense(state *State) error { /* ... */ }\nfunc (h *postCommitActionHandler) HandleWarnStaleSession(state *State) error { return nil } // explicit no-op\n```\n\n**Key benefit**: Add a new `Action` → add a method to `ActionHandler` → compiler error at every callsite that doesn't implement it.\n\n## Alternatives Considered\n\n| Approach | Compile-time safe? | Notes |\n| -- | -- | -- |\n| **Interface** (proposed) | Yes | Most Go-idiomatic for this; small interface (5 methods) |\n| `exhaustive` linter | Partially | Already enabled; catches caller switches but NOT the framework's routing gap in `ApplyCommonActions` |\n| **Struct of func fields** | No (runtime) | Less ceremony but nil-field checks are runtime only |\n| **Single strategy action enum** | No | Each transition has ≤1 strategy action, but still no switch exhaustiveness |\n\n## Scope\n\n* Introduce `ActionHandler` interface in `session/phase.go`\n* Replace `ApplyCommonActions` → `ApplyTransition` (framework calls handler methods)\n* Refactor `PostCommit` dispatch loop in `manual_commit_hooks.go` to use handler struct\n* Update any other callers of `ApplyCommonActions`\n* Existing tests should continue passing (behavior unchanged)\n\n## Context\n\n* PR #172: Phase-aware PostCommit (where this was identified)\n* Commits `eafc951` and `9e64962`: Fixed the immediate bug (condensation failure orphaning shadow branches) and added test coverage for the dispatch loop\n* The dispatch loop now has comprehensive tests (7 new cases), so this refactor has a safety > AGENT

Ha — you already identified this exact class of bug. ENT-250 describes the silent-drop risk: callers dispatch actions in a `switch` with no exhaustiveness guarantee. The `transitionSessionTurnEnd` case is the most extreme version — it doesn't even have a switch, it just drops everything.

The `ActionHandler` interface would prevent this entirely — if the stop hook needs to handle `TurnEnd`, it'd need an `ActionHandler` implementation, and the compiler would force it to handle `ActionCondense`.

So the immediate fix for #172 is to wire up condensation in `transitionSessionTurnEnd`, and ENT-250 is the longer-term refactor to make these silent drops impossible. Let me reference ENT-250 in the comment.

     1→# ENT-221 + ENT-194: Session Phase State Machine (v2)
     2→
     3→> **For Claude:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task.
     4→
     5→**Goal:** Introduce a session phase state machine so hooks can distinguish "agent committed mid-session" from "user committed between sessions", preventing premature condensation and data loss.
     6→
     7→**Architecture:** Add a Phase field to session state that tracks the session lifecycle (ACTIVE, ACTIVE_COMMITTED, IDLE, ENDED). Git hooks check the phase before deciding whether to condense.
     8→
     9→**Tech Stack:** Go, go-git v5
    10→
    11→**Supersedes:** `docs/plans/2026-02-06-session-phase-state-machine.md` (v1)
    12→**Review notes:** `docs/plans/2026-02-06-session-phase-review-notes.md`
    13→
    14→---
    15→
    16→## Terminology
    17→
    18→- **Checkpoint** = data condensed to `entire/checkpoints/v1`, linked to a user commit
    19→  via `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer. Permanent storage. Created at commit time.
    20→- **Step** = shadow branch commit, one per SaveChanges (each agent turn). Rewindable.
    21→  Ephemeral until condensed into a checkpoint.
    22→
    23→A checkpoint may contain multiple steps' worth of data. The shadow branch accumulates
    24→steps until the user commits, at which point they are condensed into a checkpoint.
    25→
    26→---
    27→
    28→## Context
    29→
    30→When an AI agent commits via Bash mid-session (between UserPromptSubmit and Stop hooks), `post-commit` fires and prematurely condenses session data, resets step count, and deletes the shadow branch. This causes:
    31→
    32→- **ENT-194**: Sequential agent commits produce empty/incomplete checkpoints because each `post-commit` condenses before the transcript is complete
    33→- **ENT-221**: No cross-hook state tracking means hooks can't distinguish "agent committed mid-session" from "user committed between sessions"
    34→
    35→The fix introduces a **session phase state machine** so hooks know the session's lifecycle stage.
    36→
    37→**Note:** File locking for concurrent hook access is deferred to ENT-238 (SQLite migration).
    38→The current atomic write-then-rename approach is retained, with a known narrow race window
    39→for concurrent hook processes.
    40→
    41→## State Machine
    42→
    43→### States
    44→
    45→| State | Description |
    46→|---|---|
    47→| **ACTIVE** | Agent is working on a turn. Set on UserPromptSubmit, cleared on Stop. |
    48→| **ACTIVE_COMMITTED** | Agent is working AND has made git commits this session. PostCommit defers condensation. |
    49→| **IDLE** | Turn finished, session still alive. Condensable on next user commit. |
    50→| **ENDED** | Session process exited. Condensable on next commit (if FilesTouched), otherwise discardable. |
    51→
    52→Note: UNINITIALIZED is not a stored state — it means no state file exists yet.
    53→Empty/missing Phase field in existing state files is treated as IDLE (backward compat).
    54→
    55→### Transitions
    56→
    57→```
    58→UNINITIALIZED ──UserPromptSubmit──────> ACTIVE           (state file created)
    59→ACTIVE ──Stop─────────────────────────> IDLE
    60→ACTIVE ──UserPromptSubmit─────────────> ACTIVE           (Ctrl-C recovery: just continue)
    61→ACTIVE ──git commit───────────────────> ACTIVE_COMMITTED
    62→ACTIVE ──SessionStop──────────────────> ENDED            (graceful shutdown, no turn completed)
    63→ACTIVE_COMMITTED ──git commit─────────> ACTIVE_COMMITTED
    64→ACTIVE_COMMITTED ──Stop───────────────> IDLE             ← triggers condense action
    65→ACTIVE_COMMITTED ──SessionStop────────> ENDED            (agent died after committing)
    66→IDLE ──git commit─────────────────────> IDLE             ← triggers condense action
    67→IDLE ──UserPromptSubmit───────────────> ACTIVE
    68→IDLE ──SessionStop────────────────────> ENDED
    69→ENDED ──SessionStart (re-entry)───────> IDLE             (clear EndedAt, immediately condensable)
    70→ENDED ──git commit────────────────────> ENDED            ← triggers condense/discard action
    71→IDLE/ENDED ──UserPromptSubmit─────────> ACTIVE           (clear EndedAt if needed)
    72→```
    73→
    74→Condensation is an **action** triggered by certain transitions, not a state. The state
    75→machine declares `ActionCondense` (or `ActionCondenseIfFilesTouched` / `ActionDiscardIfNoFiles`)
    76→in the transition result; the caller executes it. See the transition table in Task 1 for
    77→the full action mapping.
    78→
    79→**SessionStart re-entry:** When `SessionStart` fires and a state file exists:
    80→- Phase = ENDED → set Phase = IDLE, clear EndedAt (session re-entered, immediately condensable)
    81→- Phase = IDLE → no-op (already condensable)
    82→- Phase = ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED → leave as-is (warn user about stale session)
    83→- No state file → UNINITIALIZED (wait for UserPromptSubmit to create state)
    84→
    85→### Key Behaviors
    86→
    87→- **ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED**: `post-commit` defers condensation, only updates BaseCommit + migrates shadow branch
    88→- **ACTIVE_COMMITTED → IDLE**: Stop triggers immediate condensation (agent's commits already exist on branch)
    89→- **ACTIVE → ACTIVE (Ctrl-C recovery)**: Just reset to ACTIVE for new turn. No catch-up checkpoint. Interrupted turn's transcript data folds into next step naturally.
    90→- **ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED → ENDED (SessionStop)**: Graceful shutdown without a completed turn. Shadow branch data preserved, condensable on next commit or via `entire sessions fix`.
    91→- **Shadow branch deletion**: Only when ALL sessions on the branch are condensed or discarded
    92→- **PendingCheckpointID**: Generated once per checkpoint cycle, shared across all commits in a session
    93→- **Rebase/merge detection**: PostCommit skips phase transitions during sequence operations (`.git/rebase-merge/` or `.git/rebase-apply/` present)
    94→
    95→### Condensation Eligibility
    96→
    97→| Phase | FilesTouched? | Action |
    98→|---|---|---|
    99→| ACTIVE / IDLE | Any | **Condense** (session ongoing, context valuable) |
   100→| ENDED | Non-empty | **Condense** (contributed to code) |
   101→| ENDED | Empty | **Discard** (no code contribution, noise) |
   102→
   103→**Simplified rule:** Discard only when `ENDED AND len(FilesTouched) == 0`.
   104→
   105→Additionally, users can explicitly remove a session from checkpointing via `entire reset --session <id>`. This clears the session state; any file changes remain in the working directory for the user to handle via git.
   106→
   107→### Stale Session Detection
   108→
   109→No automatic timeout detection. Instead:
   110→
   111→- **SessionStart warning**: If other sessions exist with no interaction in ~hours, show:
   112→  `"Found N session(s) with no recent activity. Run 'entire sessions fix' to resolve."`
   113→- **`entire sessions fix`**: User-initiated command. Scans for sessions in pathological states
   114→  (ACTIVE_COMMITTED with no running agent, old ENDED sessions). Shows session info (phase,
   115→  last seen, shadow branch data). Lets user choose per session: Condense / Discard / Skip.
   116→- **`entire status`**: Enhanced to show session phases and stuck states.
   117→
   118→**Rationale:** TTL-based detection causes false positives (long builds, permission prompts,
   119→complex reasoning). Users can determine session liveness better than any heuristic.
   120→
   121→### `LastInteractionTime`
   122→
   123→Updated on **every hook invocation** — UserPromptSubmit, Stop, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, etc.
   124→Provides accurate "last seen" signal for the `entire sessions fix` UI and SessionStart warning.
   125→
   126→### Known Limitations
   127→
   128→**Ctrl-C interruption:** When a user Ctrl-C's during agent work, no hook fires. The session
   129→stays in ACTIVE. On next UserPromptSubmit → ACTIVE → ACTIVE transition → just continue.
   130→The interrupted turn gets no rewind point (step), but its transcript lines fold into the next
   131→step. Files modified during the interrupted turn are captured via `git status` in subsequent
   132→steps, though without fine-grained transcript attribution.
   133→
   134→**ACTIVE_COMMITTED + dead agent:** If an agent commits mid-session and then crashes (no Stop
   135→hook fires), the session is stuck in ACTIVE_COMMITTED. PostCommit will always defer for this
   136→session. Resolution: user runs `entire sessions fix` to condense or discard. Data is safe on
   137→the shadow branch until resolved.
   138→
   139→**Backward compatibility:** Existing sessions without a Phase field are treated as IDLE
   140→(empty → IDLE). In-flight sessions at code update time don't get the fix — they experience
   141→the same premature condensation bug that already exists. Only sessions started after the
   142→update benefit from phase tracking.
   143→

   149→PR 1: Pure State Machine + Phase Types + Transcript Fields + Type Consolidation
   150→  → Tasks 1 + 2 + 3, with exhaustive unit tests
   151→  → Pure logic only, no behavior change, no hook wiring
   152→
   153→PR 2: Wire State Machine into Hooks
   154→  → Task 4, with unit + integration tests for phase transitions
   155→
   156→PR 3: Phase-Aware Git Hooks (the actual bug fix)
   157→  → Tasks 5 + 6, with integration tests for mid-session commits
   158→
   159→PR 4: Cleanup + Polish + Doctor Command
   160→  → Tasks 7 + 8 + 9 + 10 + 11, with remaining tests + docs
   161→```
   162→
   163→Each PR ships with its own tests. PRs are independently reviewable and deployable in order.
   164→
   165→**Key insight:** PR 1 builds and exhaustively tests the state machine as a **pure function**
   166→(`Transition(phase, event) → result`) with no side effects. This means the core logic can be
   167→validated with table-driven tests before any hook wiring. PRs 2-3 then wire it in and add
   168→integration tests.

   171→
   172→## Task 1: Pure State Machine (PR 1)
   173→
   174→Build the state machine as a standalone, pure-function component. No side effects, no file I/O,
   175→no git operations. Just `(currentPhase, event) → (newPhase, actions)`.
   176→
   177→**Files:**
   178→- Create: `cmd/entire/cli/session/phase.go` — Phase type, Event type, Action type, `Transition()` function, `MermaidDiagram()` generator
   179→- Create: `cmd/entire/cli/session/phase_test.go` — Exhaustive table-driven tests for all transitions + diagram generation test
   180→
   181→**Types in `session/phase.go`:**
   182→```go
   183→package session
   184→
   185→// Phase represents the lifecycle stage of a session.
   186→type Phase string
   187→
   188→const (
   189→    PhaseActive          Phase = "active"
   190→    PhaseActiveCommitted Phase = "active_committed"
   191→    PhaseIdle            Phase = "idle"
   192→    PhaseEnded           Phase = "ended"
   193→)
   194→
   195→// PhaseFromString normalizes a phase string, treating empty as PhaseIdle
   196→// for backward compatibility with pre-state-machine session files.
   197→func PhaseFromString(s string) Phase {
   198→    switch Phase(s) {
   199→    case PhaseActive, PhaseActiveCommitted, PhaseIdle, PhaseEnded:
   200→        return Phase(s)
   201→    default:
   202→        return PhaseIdle // empty or unknown → idle (backward compat)
   203→    }
   204→}
   205→
   206→func (p Phase) IsActive() bool {
   207→    return p == PhaseActive || p == PhaseActiveCommitted
   208→}
   209→
   210→// Event represents something that happened to a session.
   211→type Event int
   212→
   213→const (
   214→    EventUserPromptSubmit Event = iota // Agent received a new user prompt
   215→    EventStop                          // Agent turn ended (Stop hook)
   216→    EventGitCommit                     // A git commit was made (PostCommit hook)
   217→    EventSessionStart                  // Session process started (SessionStart hook)
   218→    EventSessionStop                   // Session process ended (SessionStop hook)
   219→)
   220→
   221→// Action represents a side effect that should be performed after a transition.
   222→// The caller is responsible for executing these — the state machine only declares them.
   223→type Action int
   224→
   225→const (
   226→    ActionCondense              Action = iota // Condense session data to permanent storage
   227→    ActionCondenseIfFilesTouched              // Condense only if FilesTouched is non-empty
   228→    ActionDiscardIfNoFiles                    // Discard session if FilesTouched is empty
   229→    ActionMigrateShadowBranch                // Migrate shadow branch to new HEAD
   230→    ActionWarnStaleSession                   // Warn user about stale session(s)
   231→    ActionClearEndedAt                       // Clear EndedAt timestamp (session re-entering)
   232→    ActionUpdateLastInteraction              // Update LastInteractionTime
   233→)
   234→
   235→// TransitionResult holds the outcome of a state machine transition.
   236→type TransitionResult struct {
   237→    NewPhase Phase
   238→    Actions  []Action
   239→}
   240→
   241→// Transition computes the next phase and required actions given the current
   242→// phase and an event. This is a pure function with no side effects.
   243→//
   244→// Context parameters (like FilesTouched length or whether a rebase is in
   245→// progress) are passed via TransitionContext to keep the function pure
   246→// while allowing context-dependent transitions.
   247→func Transition(current Phase, event Event, ctx TransitionContext) TransitionResult {
   248→    // ... implementation
   249→}
   250→
   251→// TransitionContext provides read-only context for transitions that need
   252→// to inspect session state without mutating it.
   253→type TransitionContext struct {
   254→    HasFilesTouched bool // len(FilesTouched) > 0
   255→    IsRebaseInProgress bool // .git/rebase-merge/ or .git/rebase-apply/ exists
   256→}
   257→```
   258→
   259→**Transition table (implemented in `Transition()`):**
   260→
   261→| Current Phase | Event | Context | New Phase | Actions |
   262→|---|---|---|---|---|
   263→| `""` (empty) | any | — | treated as IDLE | (see IDLE rows) |
   264→| IDLE | UserPromptSubmit | — | ACTIVE | [UpdateLastInteraction] |
   265→| IDLE | GitCommit | rebase=false | IDLE | [Condense, UpdateLastInteraction] |
   266→| IDLE | GitCommit | rebase=true | IDLE | [] (skip everything) |
   267→| IDLE | SessionStop | — | ENDED | [UpdateLastInteraction] |
   268→| IDLE | SessionStart | — | IDLE | [] (no-op, already condensable) |
   269→| ACTIVE | UserPromptSubmit | — | ACTIVE | [UpdateLastInteraction] (Ctrl-C recovery) |
   270→| ACTIVE | Stop | — | IDLE | [UpdateLastInteraction] |
   271→| ACTIVE | GitCommit | rebase=false | ACTIVE_COMMITTED | [MigrateShadowBranch, UpdateLastInteraction] |
   272→| ACTIVE | GitCommit | rebase=true | ACTIVE | [] (skip everything) |
   273→| ACTIVE | SessionStop | — | ENDED | [UpdateLastInteraction] |
   274→| ACTIVE | SessionStart | — | ACTIVE | [WarnStaleSession] |
   275→| ACTIVE_COMMITTED | Stop | — | IDLE | [Condense, UpdateLastInteraction] |
   276→| ACTIVE_COMMITTED | GitCommit | rebase=false | ACTIVE_COMMITTED | [MigrateShadowBranch, UpdateLastInteraction] |
   277→| ACTIVE_COMMITTED | GitCommit | rebase=true | ACTIVE_COMMITTED | [] (skip everything) |
   278→| ACTIVE_COMMITTED | UserPromptSubmit | — | ACTIVE | [UpdateLastInteraction] (Ctrl-C recovery after commit) |
   279→| ACTIVE_COMMITTED | SessionStop | — | ENDED | [UpdateLastInteraction] |
   280→| ACTIVE_COMMITTED | SessionStart | — | ACTIVE_COMMITTED | [WarnStaleSession] |
   281→| ENDED | UserPromptSubmit | — | ACTIVE | [ClearEndedAt, UpdateLastInteraction] |
   282→| ENDED | GitCommit | files=true, rebase=false | ENDED | [CondenseIfFilesTouched, UpdateLastInteraction] |
   283→| ENDED | GitCommit | files=false, rebase=false | ENDED | [DiscardIfNoFiles, UpdateLastInteraction] |
   284→| ENDED | GitCommit | rebase=true | ENDED | [] (skip everything) |
   285→| ENDED | SessionStart | — | IDLE | [ClearEndedAt] (re-entry) |
   286→
   287→**Mermaid diagram generation (`phase.go`):**
   288→
   289→```go
   290→// MermaidDiagram generates a Mermaid state diagram from the transition table.
   291→// The diagram is derived by calling Transition() for all (phase, event, context)
   292→// combinations, so it's always in sync with the implementation.
   293→func MermaidDiagram() string {
   294→    // Iterate all phases × events × context variants
   295→    // Call Transition() for each, collect edges
   296→    // Format as Mermaid stateDiagram-v2
   297→    // ...
   298→}
   299→```
   300→
   301→The generator iterates every `(Phase, Event, TransitionContext)` combination, calls
   302→`Transition()`, and formats the results as a Mermaid `stateDiagram-v2`. Edge labels
   303→include the event name and actions (if any). Since the diagram is derived from the
   304→actual `Transition()` function, it can never drift from the implementation.
   305→
   306→**Tests (`phase_test.go`):**
   307→- Table-driven: one row per transition in the table above
   308→- Edge cases: empty string phase → treated as IDLE
   309→- Verify that rebase context always produces empty actions
   310→- Verify all phase+event combinations are covered (no panics/undefined behavior)
   311→- Verify Action slice contents exactly (order matters for execution)
   312→- `TestMermaidDiagram`: calls `MermaidDiagram()`, verifies it contains expected nodes
   313→  and edges, writes output to `docs/plans/session-phase-state-machine.mmd`
   314→
   315→**Verification:** `mise run fmt && mise run lint && mise run test`

   403→## Task 4: Wire State Machine into Hooks (PR 2)

   405→Connect hook handlers to the `Transition()` function. Each hook constructs an Event,

   408→**Files:**

   410→- Modify: `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go` — `InitializeSession()`: call `Transition(phase, EventUserPromptSubmit, ctx)`, set phase=result.NewPhase, dispatch actions
   411→- Modify: `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_git.go` — `SaveChanges()`: update LastInteractionTime
   412→- Modify: `cmd/entire/cli/hooks_claudecode_handlers.go` — `commitWithMetadata()` (Stop handler): call `Transition(phase, EventStop, ctx)`, dispatch actions (condense if ACTIVE_COMMITTED→IDLE)
   413→- Modify: `cmd/entire/cli/hooks_claudecode_handlers.go` — `markSessionEnded()`: call `Transition(phase, EventSessionStop, ctx)`, set phase=ENDED
   414→- Modify: `cmd/entire/cli/hooks_claudecode_handlers.go` — all hook handlers: dispatch ActionUpdateLastInteraction
   415→
   416→**Action dispatch pattern:**
   417→```go
   418→result := session.Transition(state.Phase, event, session.TransitionContext{
   419→    HasFilesTouched:    len(state.FilesTouched) > 0,
   420→    IsRebaseInProgress: isRebaseInProgress(),
   421→})
   422→state.Phase = result.NewPhase
   423→
   424→for _, action := range result.Actions {
   425→    switch action {
   426→    case session.ActionCondense:
   427→        // ... call condenseSession()
   428→    case session.ActionMigrateShadowBranch:
   429→        // ... call migrateShadowBranchIfNeeded()
   430→    case session.ActionUpdateLastInteraction:
   431→        now := time.Now()
   432→        state.LastInteractionTime = &now
   433→    case session.ActionClearEndedAt:
   434→        state.EndedAt = nil
   435→    case session.ActionWarnStaleSession:
   436→        // ... print warning
   437→    }
   438→}
   439→```
   440→
   441→**InitializeSession changes:**
   442→- Calls `Transition(phase, EventUserPromptSubmit, ctx)` to get the correct phase
   443→- IDLE/ENDED → ACTIVE: normal start
   444→- ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED → ACTIVE: Ctrl-C recovery, just continue
   445→

   447→- Calls `Transition(phase, EventStop, ctx)` after SaveChanges
   448→- If actions include ActionCondense → condense immediately (was ACTIVE_COMMITTED)
   449→- Phase always becomes IDLE after Stop

   455→## Task 5: Phase-Aware PostCommit (PR 3)
   456→
   457→Update `PostCommit()` to call `Transition()` for each session and dispatch actions.
   458→
   459→**Files:**
   460→- Modify: `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go` — `PostCommit()`: phase-aware condensation logic via Transition()
   461→- Modify: `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_migration.go` — Ensure `migrateShadowBranchIfNeeded` works when called from PostCommit context
   462→
   463→**PostCommit logic:**
   464→```go
   465→for each session on this shadow branch:
   466→    result := session.Transition(state.Phase, session.EventGitCommit, session.TransitionContext{
   467→        HasFilesTouched:    len(state.FilesTouched) > 0,
   468→        IsRebaseInProgress: isRebaseInProgress(),
   469→    })
   470→    state.Phase = result.NewPhase
   471→
   472→    for _, action := range result.Actions {
   473→        switch action {
   474→        case session.ActionCondense:
   475→            condense(state)
   476→        case session.ActionCondenseIfFilesTouched:
   477→            if len(state.FilesTouched) > 0 { condense(state) }
   478→        case session.ActionDiscardIfNoFiles:
   479→            if len(state.FilesTouched) == 0 { discard(state) }
   480→        case session.ActionMigrateShadowBranch:
   481→            migrateShadowBranch(state)
   482→        }
   483→    }
   484→```
   485→
   486→**Shadow branch deletion:**
   487→```
   488→canDelete = true
   489→for each session on this shadow branch:
   490→    if session.Phase.IsActive():
   491→        canDelete = false
   492→if canDelete:
   493→    delete shadow branch
   494→```
   495→
   496→Note: For single-session workflows (the common case), the "check all sessions" logic is
   497→trivial — there's only one session. The enumeration only matters for concurrent sessions.
   498→
   499→**Verification:** `mise run fmt && mise run lint && mise run test`

   503→## Task 6: Phase-Aware PrepareCommitMsg + Amend Fix (PR 3)
   504→
   505→Update `PrepareCommitMsg()` to use `PendingCheckpointID` from session state and fix the
   506→`git commit --amend` trailer loss bug.
   507→
   508→**Files:**
   509→- Modify: `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go` — `PrepareCommitMsg()`: use PendingCheckpointID, fix amend handling
   510→
   511→**Logic:**
   512→```
   513→# Rebase/merge: skip entirely (existing behavior)
   514→if source == "merge" or "squash":
   515→    return
   516→
   517→# Amend: preserve or restore trailer
   518→if source == "commit":
   519→    if message already has Entire-Checkpoint trailer:
   520→        return (keep it)
   521→    if any session has PendingCheckpointID:
   522→        add trailer with PendingCheckpointID
   523→        return
   524→    return (no checkpoint to link)
   525→
   526→# Normal commit (existing behavior + PendingCheckpointID)
   527→if any session is ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED with PendingCheckpointID:
   528→    use it
   529→else if sessions have new content:
   530→    generate new PendingCheckpointID, store in state
   531→    use it
   532→else if sessions have LastCheckpointID:
   533→    reuse it
   534→```
   535→
   536→**Current bug fixed:** PrepareCommitMsg previously returned early for `source="commit"`
   537→(amend), skipping entirely. Code to preserve existing trailers was unreachable. When users
   538→amended with `-m`, the trailer was lost. Now PendingCheckpointID in session state is the
   539→source of truth, and the trailer is restored even if `-m` strips it.
   540→
   541→**Verification:** `mise run fmt && mise run lint && mise run test`

   562→## Task 8: `entire sessions fix` Command (PR 4)
   563→
   564→Add user-initiated command for resolving stuck sessions.
   565→
   566→**Files:**

   568→- Modify: `cmd/entire/cli/commands/root.go` (or command registration) — Register new command

   570→**Logic:**
   571→```
   572→entire sessions fix:
   573→  1. Scan all session states via StateStore.List()
   574→  2. Identify pathological sessions:
   575→     - ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED with no recent LastInteractionTime
   576→     - ENDED with uncondensed shadow branch data
   577→  3. For each, display:
   578→     - Session ID, phase, last interaction time
   579→     - Shadow branch status (exists? has data?)
   580→     - Files touched
   581→  4. Prompt user: [Condense] [Discard] [Skip]
   582→     - Condense: run condensation, transition to IDLE, clean up
   583→     - Discard: clear state file, delete shadow branch if no other sessions need it
   584→     - Skip: leave as-is
   585→```

   591→## Task 9: Targeted Session Reset + Reset Guards (PR 4)
   592→
   593→Add `--session` flag to `entire reset` and guards for active sessions.

   598→
   599→**Logic:**
   600→```
   601→entire reset --session <id>:
   602→  1. Load session state by ID
   603→  2. Clear session state file
   604→  3. If no other sessions reference the shadow branch → delete shadow branch
   605→  4. If other sessions still need it → leave shadow branch
   606→  5. File changes remain in working directory (user handles via git)
   607→
   608→entire reset (no args):
   609→  If any session has phase ACTIVE or ACTIVE_COMMITTED:
   610→    warn: "Active sessions detected. Wait for them to finish or run
   611→           'entire sessions fix' first. Use --force to override."
   612→    require --force to proceed
   613→```

   662→
   663→## Edge Cases: External Git Operations
   664→
   665→### `entire reset` while session is ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED
   666→
   667→Warn and require `--force`. If forced: shadow branch deleted, state cleared. Agent
   668→self-heals on next SaveChanges (creates new shadow branch, fresh state). Produces split
   669→data — document that users should wait for session to finish or run `entire sessions fix`.
   670→
   671→### `git stash` while IDLE
   672→
   673→HEAD unchanged, no hooks fire. Shadow branch + session state untouched. `git stash pop`
   674→restores files. **Safe.**
   675→
   676→### `git reset --hard` (to HEAD) while IDLE
   677→
   678→Cleans working directory, HEAD unchanged. Agent's changes gone from working directory but
   679→**preserved on shadow branch**. User can `entire rewind` to restore. **Safe.**
   680→
   681→### `git reset --hard <older-commit>` while IDLE
   682→
   683→HEAD moves backward, no hooks fire. On next `UserPromptSubmit` →
   684→`migrateShadowBranchIfNeeded()` renames shadow branch. **Collision risk** if older commit
   685→already has a shadow branch (pre-existing issue, out of scope).
   686→
   687→### `git rebase` while ACTIVE
   688→
   689→PostCommit detects `.git/rebase-merge/` or `.git/rebase-apply/` and **skips entirely**.
   690→No phase transitions, no shadow branch migration. After rebase completes, next
   691→UserPromptSubmit or Stop handles the HEAD change via normal migration. **Safe.**
   692→
   693→### `git commit --amend`
   694→
   695→PrepareCommitMsg restores `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer from `PendingCheckpointID` in
   696→session state, even if `-m` flag stripped the original trailer. PostCommit defers for
   697→ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED sessions as normal. **Fixed (was a known limitation).**
   698→
   699→### User abandons work (git restore) then starts new session
   700→
   701→- Old session's `FilesTouched` still lists files (even though reverted)
   702→- If ENDED + FilesTouched non-empty → condensed with historical data
   703→- If user wants to fully discard → use `entire reset --session <id>`
   704→- New session starts fresh, shares shadow branch, no cross-contamination
   705→

   712→- **`entire/sessions` → `entire/checkpoints/v1` rename**: Account for the branch rename

   714→- **Auto-commit strategy**: Phase tracking is not prioritized for auto-commit. If naturally

    28→// askConfirmTTY prompts the user for a yes/no confirmation via /dev/tty.
    29→// This works even when stdin is redirected (e.g., git commit -m).
    30→// Returns true for yes, false for no. If TTY is unavailable, returns the default.
    31→// If context is non-empty, it is displayed on a separate line before the prompt.
    32→func askConfirmTTY(prompt string, context string, defaultYes bool) bool {
    33→	// Open /dev/tty for both reading and writing
    34→	// This is the controlling terminal, which works even when stdin/stderr are redirected
    35→	tty, err := os.OpenFile("/dev/tty", os.O_RDWR, 0)
    36→	if err != nil {
    37→		// Can't open TTY (e.g., running in CI), use default
    38→		return defaultYes
    39→	}
    40→	defer tty.Close()
    41→
    42→	// Show context if provided
    43→	if context != "" {
    44→		fmt.Fprintf(tty, "%s\n", context)
    45→	}
    46→
    47→	// Show prompt with default indicator
    48→	// Write to tty directly, not stderr, since git hooks may redirect stderr to /dev/null
    49→	var hint string
    50→	if defaultYes {
    51→		hint = "[Y/n]"
    52→	} else {
    53→		hint = "[y/N]"
    54→	}
    55→	fmt.Fprintf(tty, "%s %s ", prompt, hint)
    56→
    57→	// Read response
    58→	reader := bufio.NewReader(tty)
    59→	response, err := reader.ReadString('\n')
    60→	if err != nil {
    61→		return defaultYes
    62→	}
    63→
    64→	response = strings.TrimSpace(strings.ToLower(response))
    65→	switch response {
    66→	case "y", "yes":
    67→		return true
    68→	case "n", "no":
    69→		return false
    70→	default:
    71→		// Empty or invalid input - use default
    72→		return defaultYes
    73→	}
    74→}

    76→// CommitMsg is called by the git commit-msg hook after the user edits the message.
    77→// If the message contains only our trailer (no actual user content), strip it
    78→// so git will abort the commit due to empty message.
    79→//
    80→//nolint:unparam // error return required by interface but hooks must return nil
    81→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) CommitMsg(commitMsgFile string) error {
    82→	content, err := os.ReadFile(commitMsgFile) //nolint:gosec // Path comes from git hook
    83→	if err != nil {
    84→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
    85→	}
    86→
    87→	message := string(content)
    88→
    89→	// Check if our trailer is present (ParseCheckpoint validates format, so found==true means valid)
    90→	if _, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(message); !found {
    91→		// No trailer, nothing to do
    92→		return nil
    93→	}
    94→
    95→	// Check if there's any user content (non-comment, non-trailer lines)
    96→	if !hasUserContent(message) {
    97→		// No user content - strip the trailer so git aborts
    98→		message = stripCheckpointTrailer(message)
    99→		if err := os.WriteFile(commitMsgFile, []byte(message), 0o600); err != nil {
   100→			return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   101→		}
   102→	}
   103→
   104→	return nil
   105→}
   106→
   107→// hasUserContent checks if the message has any content besides comments and our trailer.
   108→func hasUserContent(message string) bool {
   109→	trailerPrefix := trailers.CheckpointTrailerKey + ":"
   110→	for _, line := range strings.Split(message, "\n") {
   111→		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
   112→		// Skip empty lines
   113→		if trimmed == "" {
   114→			continue
   115→		}
   116→		// Skip comment lines
   117→		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "#") {
   118→			continue
   119→		}
   120→		// Skip our trailer line
   121→		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, trailerPrefix) {
   122→			continue
   123→		}
   124→		// Found user content
   125→		return true
   126→	}
   127→	return false
   128→}
   129→
   130→// stripCheckpointTrailer removes the Entire-Checkpoint trailer line from the message.
   131→func stripCheckpointTrailer(message string) string {
   132→	trailerPrefix := trailers.CheckpointTrailerKey + ":"
   133→	var result []string
   134→	for _, line := range strings.Split(message, "\n") {
   135→		if !strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(line), trailerPrefix) {
   136→			result = append(result, line)
   137→		}
   138→	}
   139→	return strings.Join(result, "\n")
   140→}

   142→// isGitSequenceOperation checks if git is currently in the middle of a rebase,
   143→// cherry-pick, or revert operation. During these operations, commits are being
   144→// replayed and should not be linked to agent sessions.
   145→//
   146→// Detects:
   147→//   - rebase: .git/rebase-merge/ or .git/rebase-apply/ directories
   148→//   - cherry-pick: .git/CHERRY_PICK_HEAD file
   149→//   - revert: .git/REVERT_HEAD file
   150→func isGitSequenceOperation() bool {
   151→	// Get git directory (handles worktrees and relative paths correctly)
   152→	gitDir, err := GetGitDir()
   153→	if err != nil {
   154→		return false // Can't determine, assume not in sequence operation
   155→	}
   156→
   157→	// Check for rebase state directories
   158→	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(gitDir, "rebase-merge")); err == nil {
   159→		return true
   160→	}
   161→	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(gitDir, "rebase-apply")); err == nil {
   162→		return true
   163→	}
   164→
   165→	// Check for cherry-pick and revert state files
   166→	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(gitDir, "CHERRY_PICK_HEAD")); err == nil {
   167→		return true
   168→	}
   169→	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(gitDir, "REVERT_HEAD")); err == nil {
   170→		return true
   171→	}
   172→
   173→	return false
   174→}

   176→// PrepareCommitMsg is called by the git prepare-commit-msg hook.
   177→// Adds an Entire-Checkpoint trailer to the commit message with a stable checkpoint ID.
   178→// Only adds a trailer if there's actually new session content to condense.
   179→// The actual condensation happens in PostCommit - if the user removes the trailer,
   180→// the commit will not be linked to the session (useful for "manual" commits).
   181→// For amended commits, preserves the existing checkpoint ID.
   182→//
   183→// The source parameter indicates how the commit was initiated:
   184→//   - "" or "template": normal editor flow - adds trailer with explanatory comment
   185→//   - "message": using -m or -F flag - prompts user interactively via /dev/tty
   186→//   - "merge", "squash": skip trailer entirely (auto-generated messages)
   187→//   - "commit": amend operation - preserves existing trailer or restores from PendingCheckpointID
   188→//
   189→
   190→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) PrepareCommitMsg(commitMsgFile string, source string) error {
   191→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "checkpoint")
   192→
   193→	// Skip during rebase, cherry-pick, or revert operations
   194→	// These are replaying existing commits and should not be linked to agent sessions
   195→	if isGitSequenceOperation() {
   196→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: skipped during git sequence operation",
   197→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   198→			slog.String("source", source),
   199→		)
   200→		return nil
   201→	}
   202→
   203→	// Skip for merge and squash sources
   204→	// These are auto-generated messages - not from Claude sessions
   205→	switch source {
   206→	case "merge", "squash":
   207→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: skipped for source",
   208→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   209→			slog.String("source", source),
   210→		)
   211→		return nil
   212→	}
   213→
   214→	// Handle amend (source="commit") separately: preserve or restore trailer
   215→	if source == "commit" {
   216→		return s.handleAmendCommitMsg(logCtx, commitMsgFile)
   217→	}
   218→
   219→	repo, err := OpenRepository()
   220→	if err != nil {
   221→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   222→	}
   223→
   224→	worktreePath, err := GetWorktreePath()
   225→	if err != nil {
   226→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   227→	}
   228→
   229→	// Find all active sessions for this worktree
   230→	// We match by worktree (not BaseCommit) because the user may have made
   231→	// intermediate commits without entering new prompts, causing HEAD to diverge
   232→	sessions, err := s.findSessionsForWorktree(worktreePath)
   233→	if err != nil || len(sessions) == 0 {

   235→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: no active sessions",
   236→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   237→			slog.String("source", source),
   238→		)
   239→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Intentional: hooks must be silent on failure
   240→	}
   241→
   242→	// Check if any session has new content to condense
   243→	sessionsWithContent := s.filterSessionsWithNewContent(repo, sessions)
   244→
   245→	// Determine which checkpoint ID to use
   246→	var checkpointID id.CheckpointID
   247→	var hasNewContent bool
   248→	var reusedSession *SessionState
   249→
   250→	if len(sessionsWithContent) > 0 {

   255→		// This handles the case where user splits Claude's work across multiple commits

   259→
   260→		// Get current HEAD to filter sessions
   261→		head, err := repo.Head()
   262→		if err != nil {
   263→			return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   264→		}
   265→		currentHeadHash := head.Hash().String()
   266→
   267→		// Filter to sessions where BaseCommit matches current HEAD
   268→		// This prevents reusing checkpoint IDs from old sessions
   269→		// Note: BaseCommit is kept current both when new content is condensed (in the
   270→		// condensation process) and when no new content is found (via PostCommit when
   271→		// reusing checkpoint IDs). If none match, we don't add a trailer rather than
   272→		// falling back to old sessions which could have stale checkpoint IDs.
   273→		var currentSessions []*SessionState
   274→		for _, session := range sessions {
   275→			if session.BaseCommit == currentHeadHash {
   276→				currentSessions = append(currentSessions, session)
   277→			}

   280→		if len(currentSessions) == 0 {

   282→			// from old sessions as they may be stale

   287→				slog.Int("total_sessions", len(sessions)),

   322→	if existingCpID, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(message); found {

   335→		for _, state := range sessionsWithContent {

   361→		lastPrompt = s.getLastPrompt(repo, session)
   362→	} else if reusedSession != nil {
